comments.author: @Seventh-f6p
comments.text:
Great video. What is truly sad is that many Western Australians—and, for that matter, much of the Australian population—know very little about this history. Furthermore, Aboriginal people continue to be treated with far too little respect. As you mentioned in your video, they were driven off their traditional lands and dispossessed of their country.

More recently, the Australian public voted in a referendum on establishing an Indigenous Voice to Parliament, a proposal intended to give Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples a greater say in decisions affecting their lives. Sadly, the opposition to the proposal was fuelled by misinformation, fear and misleading claims, contributing to its rejection.

It is deeply troubling that a country so proud of its democracy and values could turn its back on its First Peoples in this way. At times, the attitude of the Australian public towards Indigenous Australians makes one wonder whether the true history of this land has ever been properly acknowledged or understood. It is a tragic irony that those who arrived on this continent as newcomers have so often treated its original inhabitants with such disregard.

comments.text:
it's always sad to hear how Indigenous people made a place habitable, yet everywhere on earth Indigenous people are under assault. Indonesia, Papa New Guinea, Brazil- to say nothing of the genocides of the past done by Canada, Australia, UK/US/France/Spain, Argentina... and all throughout Africa. Indigenous knowledge and traditions often helped the people who would eventually drive them from their land.

This is true in Arizona as well, where I am from. Thousands of years of humans purposefully collecting rainwater, making canals, to build aquifers that made the land fertile and habitable. And now? The people that stole the land and practically exterminated the peoples, are draining the Aquifers, and draining the soil of nutrients that they can't restore.

Colonialism/capitalism is like the private equity of humanity. Cashing in on habitability painstakingly built over thousands of years. Destroying the system that made it successful to begin with, to essentially turn nature into liquid cash.

I'm not moralizing, just... it certainly feels bleak. I wish Humanity was a happier story. I wish our future looked as bright as everyone in the past hoped it would look.
